_readme: Deliberate card renames and merges, so tools/data-audit.js --history can tell
'this card was intentionally renamed' apart from 'this card silently vanished'.
Add an entry ONLY when you deliberately rename or merge a card. Never add one
to silence a finding you haven't explained — that is exactly the mistake this

renames.why: Same plant. 'Goshiki' is the accepted cultivar name and 'Tricolor' a synonym, so the card was renamed to the accepted name and its photo and data refreshed. The design line had separately ported in a 'Goshiki' card, so both names briefly co-existed as duplicates at 2e91159; the r17 merge kept the accepted-name card and dropped the synonym. The surviving card records the synonym in its cvs field.

Same plant and card, dealt earlier the same day with a draft common name. Oscar pasted his own fully-researched JSON for the card immediately afterward with this common name; his data replaced the draft wholesale, including the rename.
Same plant and card, same-day rename as the Skimmia above — Oscar's own JSON superseded the draft common name.
Same plant and card, same-day rename as the two above. Oscar's supplied JSON also fixed a peak-vs-prose contradiction in the visual text (VERIFY-QUEUE 31), applied in the same commit as this rename.

Same plant, same card, same photograph — spelling only. Oscar's instruction: the plant in front of him is labelled 'Palmeter', and the deck is a floor reference, so it carries the name staff will see on the bench. The card arrived from the 2026-09-14 31-card batch as 'Pal Maleter'; that was a disclosed decision, not a typo — the supplied JSON's own uncertain note said the label read 'Palmeter' and chose the accepted name over it. RHS Plant Finder lists Pinus mugo 'Pal Maleter' (v) and no source was found that states 'Palmeter' as a formal synonym, so the accepted spelling is preserved in the card's cvs field rather than lost. The photo moved with the slug (photos/pinus-mugo-palmeter.jpg) and its CREDITS entry with it.

renames.fromLatin: Cyclamen persicum Super Serie Djix F1
renames.why: MERGE, not a rename. Two Cyclamen persicum cards existed: this branch held a Super Serie Djix F1 card with no photograph, and the deploy branch had already dealt a generic Cyclamen persicum with one. VERIFY-QUEUE 87 kept both because their visual lines contradict on flower shape (Djix points its petals DOWN, the dealt card and its photograph show them swept up), which is real evidence they are two different plants. Oscar's call on 2026-09-14 overrides that for now: "just make it a genus card generic for now" — he is revising bedding for an interview and does not need the cultivar split. The held card was removed rather than dealt; its full research survives in data/incoming/batch-2026-09-14-as-sent.json and batch-2026-09-14.json, so restoring it is a paste, not a re-research. The Djix photograph question in item 87 is therefore parked, not answered.
